glosses.notes: Used for a man marrying a woman; the female counterpart is 嫁.

examples.sentence: 村里那天办喜事，他穿着新衣服去接她进门，大家都说他总算把喜欢多年的人娶回家了。
父亲年轻时没什么钱，却一直认真工作，因为他不想让母亲跟着自己吃苦，还想早点把她娶回家。
老人提醒孙子，决定娶一个人以前，不但要看感情好不好，还要看以后有问题时两个人能不能一起过。

example_translations.translation: On the day of the wedding in the village, he put on new clothes and went to bring her home, and everyone said he had finally married the person he had loved for years.
When Father was young he had very little money, but he kept working seriously because he did not want Mother to suffer with him and hoped to marry her as soon as possible.

The old man reminded his grandson that before deciding to marry someone, he had to look not only at whether their feelings were good, but also at whether the two of them could keep living together when problems came later.

glosses.notes: Used when one thing takes the place of another and pushes the old one out.

examples.sentence: 纸上的老名单一直没更新，后来新系统开始用以后，电脑里的记录很快就把墙上那张旧表取代了。
老师说，机器可以帮大家查资料，可是不能取代自己去想，因为真正理解还是要靠人。
那家小店搬到网上以后，老板才发现低价并没有完全取代服务，很多老客人还是愿意回来找他。

example_translations.translation: The old paper list had never been updated, and once the new system started being used, the computer records quickly replaced the old chart on the wall.
The teacher said machines can help everyone look up information, but they cannot replace thinking for yourself, because real understanding still depends on people.
After that small shop moved online, the owner realized that low prices had not completely replaced service, and many longtime customers were still willing to come back to him.

glosses.notes: Refers to the charm, enjoyment, or interesting quality in something.

examples.sentence: 这位老师上课总会把旧故事讲得很有趣味，所以原来不爱听的人后来也慢慢坐到了前排。
父亲收旧钟表不是为了赚钱，而是觉得拆开再装回去很有趣味，做一晚上也不嫌累。
这家小店墙上的画看着不贵，却让原来有点冷的房间一下多了几分趣味。

example_translations.translation: This teacher always made old stories full of interest in class, so even the people who had not liked listening before slowly started sitting in the front rows.
Father collected old clocks not to make money, but because he found taking them apart and putting them back together fun, and he did not mind doing it all evening.
The paintings on the wall of this small shop did not look expensive, but they suddenly gave the room, which had felt a little cold, a bit more charm.

glosses.notes: Can mean a literal circle or ring, or the act of circling something with a pen.

examples.sentence: 她怕孩子看不清重点，就拿笔把地图上的起点圈出来，再叫他顺着线往下看。
医生看报告的时候，先把最要紧的数字圈在纸边，然后才慢慢跟家属解释问题出在哪里。
小区后面那块空地本来只围了一个小圈，后来来的人越来越多，大家才决定重新整理入口。

example_translations.translation: Afraid the child would miss the key point, she took a pen and circled the starting point on the map, then told him to follow the line downward.
When the doctor looked at the report, he first circled the most important figures on the page and only then slowly explained to the family where the problem was.
The empty lot behind the complex had originally been marked off in only a small circle, but later more and more people came, so everyone decided to reorganize the entrance.

glosses.notes: Used to mean from beginning to end, during the entire process or trip.

examples.sentence: 这次上山的路虽然不算远，导游还是提醒大家全程不要掉队，免得一转弯就找不到人。
记者全程站在雨里看完比赛，回去写文章的时候，连最后一次换人都没有记错。
孩子做检查时一直很紧张，母亲就全程握着他的手，直到医生说已经结束了。

example_translations.translation: Although the road up the mountain was not very long this time, the guide still reminded everyone not to fall behind for the whole trip, in case someone disappeared after one turn.
The reporter stood in the rain for the entire match, and when he went back to write the article, he did not even misremember the last substitution.
The child stayed nervous during the examination, so his mother held his hand the whole time until the doctor said it was over.

glosses.notes: Refers to the authority to decide, control, or direct other people or affairs.

examples.sentence: 负责人手里虽然有安排工作的权力，他每次改计划以前，还是会先把理由讲清楚。
父亲退休以后才发现，真正让人安心的不是说话的权力，而是家里人在难的时候还愿意信你。
老板把太多权力都放在一个人手里以后，小问题也没人敢自己处理，最后越拖越大。

example_translations.translation: Although the person in charge had the authority to arrange the work, he still explained his reasons clearly before changing the plan each time.
After Father retired, he discovered that what really brings peace of mind is not the power to have the final say, but that your family is still willing to trust you in hard times.
After the boss placed too much power in one person's hands, nobody dared handle even small problems on their own, and in the end everything got dragged out and grew bigger.

glosses.notes: A general word for tickets, coupons, or vouchers that can be used for entry or discounts.

examples.sentence: 她本来想直接买票，后来看到手机里还有一张旧优惠券，就站在门口先试着用了一下。
活动开始前，工作人员一边检查大家手里的入场券，一边提醒后面的人把包提前打开。
父亲整理柜子时翻出一张过期的优惠券，才想起那家开了很多年的小店去年已经关门了。

example_translations.translation: She had planned to buy a ticket directly, but then saw there was still an old discount coupon on her phone and tried using it first at the entrance.
Before the event started, the staff checked the admission tickets in everyone's hands while reminding the people behind them to open their bags in advance.
While Father was tidying the cabinet, he found an expired coupon and only then remembered that the little shop that had been open for many years had closed last year.

glosses.notes: A weakness, flaw, or built-in defect in a thing, design, or person.

examples.sentence: 这台机器用了半年才露出缺陷，一到晚上连续工作久一点，里面就会发出很大的声音。
他不是不知道自己太急这个缺陷，只是每次事情一多，就又把答应过的话忘了。
老师看完整篇文章以后，没有只指出语言缺陷，还告诉她哪一段其实已经写得很有力量。

example_translations.translation: This machine did not reveal its defect until it had been used for half a year; once it worked for a while at night, it started making a very loud noise inside.
It was not that he did not know that being too impatient was one of his flaws; it was just that whenever too many things piled up, he forgot what he had promised again.
After reading the whole piece, the teacher did not only point out flaws in the language, but also told her which passage had actually been written with real strength.

glosses.notes: Used for firmly setting up a system, relationship, position, or plan.

examples.sentence: 新负责人来了以后，没有马上改制度，而是先和大家谈了几次，才慢慢确立新的分工办法。
医生看完几次检查结果，才确立这个治疗计划，因为他不想让家属白白多花钱。
他们搬进新办公室以后，先花了一个月确立工作流程，后来出问题的时候才没有太乱。

example_translations.translation: After the new person in charge arrived, he did not change the system at once and instead spoke with everyone several times before gradually establishing a new division of work.
Only after seeing several sets of test results did the doctor establish this treatment plan, because he did not want the family to spend extra money for nothing.
After moving into the new office, they spent a month establishing the work process first, and that was why things were not too chaotic later when problems came up.

glosses.notes: Refers to ordinary people gathered together, especially in a public scene.

examples.sentence: 火车站外突然下起大雨，工作人员只好先把群众引到里面，再一排一排地放人进去。
演出还没开始，门口已经站满了等着进场的群众，连卖水的人都忙得顾不上休息。
出事以后，周围的群众很快走了过来，有人帮着打电话，有人主动把路先让开。

example_translations.translation: It suddenly began to rain hard outside the train station, so the staff first guided the crowd inside and then let people in row by row.
The performance had not even started, but the entrance was already full of people waiting to go in, and even the people selling water were too busy to rest.
After the incident, the crowd nearby quickly came over; some people helped make phone calls, and others moved aside to clear the way first.

glosses.notes: Material such as oil, gas, coal, or wood that is burned to create heat or power.

examples.sentence: 山上的旧车站冬天特别冷，所以工作人员每次入夜前都要先把第二天要用的燃料准备好。
司机发现油表降得比平时快，才想到可能不是路太远，而是车里的燃料正在慢慢漏掉。
老人年轻时做饭常得先搬燃料回家，现在孩子按一下开关就有火，她每次想到都觉得变化太大。

example_translations.translation: The old station on the mountain is especially cold in winter, so before night falls the staff always prepare the fuel needed for the next day.
When the driver noticed the fuel gauge dropping faster than usual, he realized the problem might not be that the road was too long, but that fuel in the vehicle was slowly leaking out.
When the old woman was young, she often had to carry fuel home before cooking; now the children just press a switch for a flame, and every time she thinks of it, the change feels enormous.

glosses.notes: Used for dyeing cloth or for something being stained with color.

examples.sentence: 她怕白衣服再被雨水染脏，刚进门就先拿纸把包上的水一点点擦干。
老人年轻时在小厂里帮人染布，所以一看颜色深浅，就知道这一盆水里是不是还要加东西。
孩子把画画的水打翻以后，桌子上的布一下就被红色染成一大片，母亲只好先把它泡进盆里。

example_translations.translation: Afraid the rainwater would stain her white clothes again, she used paper to wipe the water off her bag bit by bit as soon as she came in.
When the old man was young, he helped dye cloth in a small factory, so with one look at how deep the color was, he knew whether anything still needed to be added to that basin of water.
After the child knocked over the painting water, the cloth on the table was stained red all at once, and the mother had no choice but to soak it in a basin first.

glosses.notes: Usually refers to an issue or area attracting a lot of public attention.

examples.sentence: 这周大家见面先谈的不是天气，而是那个突然上了首页的教育热点，连父亲都看了好几篇文章。
记者跑完整个市场以后才发现，真正的消费热点不是最贵的东西，而是实用又省事的小家电。
会议还没开始，门外的人已经在小声讨论今天最可能被提到的改革热点。

example_translations.translation: This week, when people met, they did not first talk about the weather, but about the education topic that had suddenly reached the front page; even Father read several articles about it.
After covering the whole market, the reporter discovered that the real consumer hot spots were not the most expensive goods, but practical small appliances that saved effort.
Before the meeting had even started, the people outside were already quietly discussing the reform topic most likely to be raised that day.

glosses.notes: Can mean literal heat, but in modern use it often means how much attention or buzz something has.

examples.sentence: 这部旧电影原来没人提，结果一个片段放出来以后，话题热度一下就高得连主角自己都没有想到。
旅游节刚开始那几天，城里的讨论热度一直往上走，连平时不太出门的人都想去看看。
老板看着新产品的热度慢慢下来，没有急着怪员工，而是先回头检查宣传哪里做得太满。

example_translations.translation: Hardly anyone used to mention this old film, but after one clip was released, the topic's level of buzz suddenly rose so much that even the lead actor had not expected it.
In the first days of the tourism festival, the level of discussion in the city kept rising, and even people who normally did not go out much wanted to go take a look.
Watching the new product's popularity slowly cool down, the boss did not rush to blame the staff and instead first looked back to check where the promotion had been overdone.

glosses.notes: Describes something currently popular, in demand, or widely chosen.

examples.sentence: 这家医院的几个热门科室一到早上就排得很满，所以很多人天没亮就先来拿号。
去年没人注意的小路，今年突然成了周末热门去处，连卖水的小店都跟着忙起来。
父亲原来想让他报最热门的专业，听完老师的话以后，还是决定先看自己真正喜欢什么。

example_translations.translation: Several popular departments in this hospital are already full of lines early in the morning, so many people come to take a number before daybreak.
A small road that nobody noticed last year suddenly became a popular weekend destination this year, and even the little shop selling water got busy because of it.
Father originally wanted him to apply for the most popular major, but after hearing the teacher out, he still decided to look first at what he truly liked.

glosses.notes: A device that heats water for washing or household use.

examples.sentence: 房东接到电话就赶过来，因为楼上的热水器突然不出热水，住在上面的人已经两天没法好好洗澡了。
冬天刚开始那几天，父亲每天睡前都要去看一眼热水器，怕它半夜又突然停掉。
工人装热水器的时候发现墙里那根旧管已经有点松，只好先关水再重新接一遍。

example_translations.translation: The landlord hurried over as soon as he got the call, because the water heater upstairs had suddenly stopped producing hot water, and the people living there had not been able to shower properly for two days.
In the first days of winter, Father went to check the water heater every night before bed, afraid it would suddenly stop again in the middle of the night.
While installing the water heater, the worker found that an old pipe inside the wall had already become loose, so he had to shut off the water first and reconnect it.

glosses.notes: A special phone line set up for reporting problems, asking for help, or getting urgent information.

examples.sentence: 这条求助热线一到晚上就特别忙，值班的人连喝口水都得看着下一通电话什么时候进来。
新闻刚发出去，举报热线不到半天就接到很多来电，工作人员只好临时多开两个座位。
母亲把医院热线贴在厨房门上，就是怕家里老人半夜不舒服的时候一着急找不到电话。

example_translations.translation: This help hotline becomes especially busy at night, and the person on duty has to keep watching for the next call even while taking a sip of water.
Not even half a day after the news came out, the reporting hotline had already received many calls, so the staff had to open two more seats temporarily.

Mother stuck the hospital hotline on the kitchen door because she was afraid that if the older people at home felt unwell in the middle of the night, panic would make them unable to find the phone number to call.

glosses.notes: Used when an issue quickly becomes the center of widespread discussion.

examples.sentence: 新规定一出来，就在家长群里被热议，连平时很少发言的人也忍不住说了几句。
这段录像昨天还没人注意，今天一早却在网上被热议，店长一开门就接了好几个电话。
方案公布以后，这个安排马上被大家热议，因为很多人都想知道以后到底由谁负责。

example_translations.translation: As soon as the new rule came out, it was hotly discussed in the parents' group, and even people who rarely spoke could not help saying a few words.
Yesterday nobody had noticed this video clip, but by early this morning it was being hotly discussed online, and the shop manager received several phone calls as soon as he opened the door.
After the plan was announced, this arrangement was immediately hotly discussed by everyone, because many people wanted to know who would actually be responsible later on.

glosses.notes: The general term for computer systems designed to perform tasks that usually require human intelligence.

examples.sentence: 公司开会谈到人工智能时，年轻员工都很兴奋，父亲却先问这些工具到底能不能真的省时间。
医院把人工智能系统放到前台试用以后，最明显的变化不是速度更快，而是排队的人没那么乱了。
老师提醒学生，人工智能可以帮你整理材料，最后怎么判断对不对，还是得你自己负责。

example_translations.translation: When artificial intelligence came up in the company meeting, the younger employees were all excited, but Father first asked whether these tools could really save time.
After the hospital put an artificial intelligence system at the front desk on trial, the clearest change was not greater speed, but that the line had become less chaotic.

The teacher reminded the students that artificial intelligence can help you organize materials, but in the end you still have to take responsibility yourself for judging whether something is right or wrong.

glosses.notes: A colloquial pronoun that often means other people, they, or the other party depending on context.

examples.sentence: 你还没把情况问清楚，就当着大家的面怪人家，难怪对方听完以后一句话也不想说。
母亲看他一直在看别人家的车，就笑着提醒他，先把自己手里的事做好，再去羡慕人家也不迟。
人家已经提前把时间告诉你了，你临时改主意以后还怪别人没等，这话怎么听都不合适。

example_translations.translation: You blamed the other side in front of everyone before even asking clearly what had happened, so it is no wonder that after hearing you out they did not want to say another word.
Seeing him keep staring at other people's car, Mother smiled and reminded him to finish his own work properly first; there would still be time later to envy other people.
They had already told you the time in advance, yet after changing your mind at the last minute you still blamed them for not waiting; however you put it, that does not sound appropriate.

glosses.notes: Used before a number or statistic to mean the average for each person.

examples.sentence: 这个小镇看着不大，去年人均收入涨得很快，所以很多年轻人又开始考虑回去工作。
店长算完钱才发现，活动那几天来店里的人虽然多，人均消费并没有比平时高多少。
医生做完统计后提醒大家，光看总数不够，还得看各区人均床位到底差了多少。

example_translations.translation: This small town does not look large, but last year per capita income rose quickly, so many young people started considering going back to work there.
Only after counting the money did the manager realize that although many people had come into the shop during those event days, per capita spending was not much higher than usual.

After finishing the statistics, the doctor reminded everyone that looking only at the total was not enough; they also had to see how much the number of beds per capita differed from district to district.

glosses.notes: An idiom describing an extremely crowded place packed with people.

examples.sentence: 节日一到，老街从路口到河边全是人山人海，连想找个地方站住都不太容易。
演唱会散场那一刻，地铁口前面已经人山人海，工作人员只好一批一批地放人下去。
他原来只想买完东西就走，没想到广场上忽然人山人海，只能跟着大家慢慢往外走。

example_translations.translation: As soon as the holiday arrived, the old street from the intersection to the riverside became a sea of people, and even finding a place to stand still was not easy.
At the moment the concert ended, the area in front of the subway entrance was already a sea of people, so the staff had no choice but to let people go down in batches.
He had only wanted to buy what he needed and leave, but he had not expected the square to suddenly become a sea of people, so he could only move out slowly with everyone else.

glosses.notes: Refers to people connected with a certain profession, group, or social circle.

examples.sentence: 负责接待的工作人员说，下午会有几位相关人士到场，所以门口的名单还得再看一遍。
医生建议家属先听听专业人士的意见，不要只因为网上几句话就急着换药。
这件事传开以后，不少业内人士都站出来解释问题到底出在哪一环。

example_translations.translation: The staff member in charge of reception said that several relevant people would arrive in the afternoon, so the list at the entrance still had to be checked again.
The doctor suggested that the family first listen to the opinion of professionals rather than rush to change the medicine because of a few words online.
After the matter spread, quite a few people in the industry stepped forward to explain which link in the process the problem had actually appeared in.

glosses.notes: Can refer to personnel work, an HR department, or staffing matters in an organization.

examples.sentence: 她把材料交到人事部门以后，原以为很快就会有消息，没想到一直等到下周才接到电话。
公司人事临时发来通知，说培训时间要整体往后推，所以很多人只好马上改车票。
父亲退休前一直做人事工作，所以公司里很多老员工的情况，他到现在还记得很清楚。

example_translations.translation: After handing her materials to the HR department, she had expected news quickly, but instead she had to wait until the following week to get a call.
The company's HR office sent a last-minute notice saying the training time would be pushed back overall, so many people had to change their train tickets immediately.
Before retiring, Father had always done personnel work, so he still remembers the situation of many older employees in the company very clearly.

glosses.notes: Describes something created by people or caused by human action rather than happening naturally.

examples.sentence: 这次停电后来查清不是机器自己坏了，而是人为操作失误，所以责任一下就清楚了。
医生看完记录以后认为，这个结果不像自然变化，更像前一天有人为改动过数据。
老人站在河边看了很久，说眼前这片直直的河道太整齐，一看就知道是人为修过的。

example_translations.translation: It was later confirmed that this power outage had not been caused by the machine breaking on its own, but by human operating error, so responsibility became clear at once.
After looking through the records, the doctor thought this result did not look like a natural change and looked more as if the data had been altered by people the day before.
The old man stood by the river for a long time and said that the straight river channel in front of him was far too neat; one look was enough to tell that it had been altered by human hands.
